A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entity-slot approach to multi-intent SLU despite substantial renaming and revision. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and both appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, intent-count and training-data analyses, and appendix experiments with larger models and five-shot ChatGPT.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, backbone comparisons, case studies and TOPv2 experiments in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: Entity-slot construction/recovery and intent-to-sub-utterance supervision match across ENSI/SII and ECLM/Chain of Intent. However, v3 explicitly uses frozen base weights with LoRA and regex extraction of generated fields; v4 describes generic supervised fine-tuning and BIO recovery without specifying these procedures. It is unclear whether they changed or their descriptions were omitted.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on a separate semantic-parsing benchmark, TOPv2, covering Alarm and Weather in Appendix A.1. MixATIS and MixSNIPS remain; dropping the LM-Mix names does not establish removal of their transformed data.

E2.justification: v4 Table 2 adds reported Stack-Propagation and RoBERTa+Linear comparisons; Stack-Propagation was previously described but absent from the results. Vanilla SFT becomes a direct comparator in Table 3. The MixATIS intent-count comparison also adds GL-GIN and non-RoBERTa CLID alongside the retained comparators.

E3.justification: The default backbone changes from the earlier 7B model configurations to Llama3.1-8B-Instruct. Section 4.2 changes the reported learning rate from 1e-4 to 2e-5, temperature from 0.1 to 0.0, and training budget from dataset-specific step counts to one epoch. ESA/CSA evaluation and five-shot testing disappear; TOPv2 introduces 20k training and 2k evaluation samples per domain.

E4.justification: v3 already compares EN against ENSI and examines intent counts, data fractions and model scale. v4 expands component testing to removing entity slots, intent chaining or both, adds four case illustrations, and examines instruction-tuned versus base backbones. It removes the larger-model analysis, MixSNIPS intent-count breakdown and data-fraction analyses of slot F1 and intent accuracy.

E5.justification: Both main-result tables use the same p < 0.05 t-test significance convention. Neither version supplies run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or dispersion estimates. The additional starred result in v4 changes the reported significance outcome, not the reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 reports best overall accuracies of 53.4% on MixATIS for EN-Mistral and 83.9% on MixSNIPS for ENSI-Mistral; v4 Table 2 reports 56.2% and 86.5% for ECLM under changed backbone and training settings. These are not isolated same-setting gains. Ablation, backbone, TOPv2 and case results are added, while ESA/CSA, larger-model, five-shot and several supplementary result entries disappear.

T1.justification: v3 Section 6's definitions of ESA and CSA are removed, eliminating its mathematical metric contribution. The LoRA decomposition and forward-pass derivation also disappear. v4's more explicit entity and sub-intent mappings mainly formalize existing descriptions; neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 emphasizes exploring LLM feasibility, two model series, reconstructed datasets and two new metrics, with competitive performance. v4 centers its contributions on ECLM and Chain of Intent, drops the dataset and metric contribution claims, and asserts superiority over conventional fine-tuning and consistent overall-accuracy advantages across intent counts.

C2.justification: v3 explains SII's mixed benefits through domain complexity and emphasizes deterioration with increasing intent counts. v4 emphasizes robustness, interprets chaining as improving joint prediction despite lower intent accuracy, and adds explanations involving O-tag imbalance and instruction tuning. LoRA and observed scaling caveats give way to a limitation about testing beyond 8B parameters. Figure 5's displayed labels contradict its new correctness interpretation.

D1.justification: v4 adds batch size, epoch count, hyperparameter search ranges, vocabulary and label statistics, and worked ECLM/Vanilla prompt comparisons. It omits v3's LoRA settings, quantization, optimizer, GPU, regex extraction details and validation counts. The advertised repository changes from SLM, described as providing code and datasets, to ECLM, described as providing code.

R1.justification: The core SLU literature remains. v4 adds Chen et al. (2020) for TOPv2, removes the LoRA and QLoRA references, and drops the explicit CLID inspiration from the renamed intent-chaining subsection. The earlier first-use positioning for LLMs in multi-intent SLU becomes more method-focused.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten around ECLM. Construction and recovery are grouped together, the research-question framing and metric section disappear, the LLM related-work discussion is substantially condensed, and the appendix is reorganized into TOPv2 experiments and case illustrations.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, and v4 adds a separate prompt-comparison figure. v3's six-panel data-ratio plot becomes a two-panel plot with numerical labels and Uni-MIS references. New dataset and ablation tables, revised comparison tables, and four case figures substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4's direct Vanilla SFT control and component ablations strengthen evidence for the entity-slot design beyond v3's EN/ENSI comparison; worked prompts and TOPv2 evaluation also help assessment. The net gain is limited by omitted implementation details and an incorrect case explanation: Figure 5 labels 'theatre is' as ECLM's location span while the prose claims 'movie theatre'. Higher headline scores also use changed settings and do not establish same-setting methodological progress.
